groups.title: Unit Testing with Vitest
groups.question: You want fast tests for your stores and helpers that do not need real secrets. Explain how you would set up Vitest.

followUps.Vitest setup and test file conventions: Why does Vitest fit a SvelteKit project?
followUps.Testing pure utility functions and store: Why are stores and helpers easy to test?
followUps.Mocking modules and environment variable: How would you mock modules and environment variables?

evidence.text: Vitest uses Vite and shares its configuration.
It supports the same import aliases as the app.
Files named .test.ts run automatically.
Stores and helpers are plain JavaScript.
They can be tested without a browser or DOM.
Such tests run quickly in Node.
vi.mock replaces a module with a test double.
Mocking the $env modules avoids needing real secrets.
Tests control what dependencies return.

groups.title: Deployment Strategies
groups.question: Your app works locally but fails on the host because of a wrong adapter and missing variables. Explain how you would deploy correctly.

followUps.Choosing an adapter for your target plat: How do you choose an adapter?
followUps.Environment variables in production depl: How are environment variables set for production?

evidence.text: The adapter must match the host, such as Vercel, Netlify or a Node server.
Each adapter produces a different build output.
A mismatched adapter causes deploy or runtime errors.
Production values are set in the hosting dashboard, not in committed .env files.
The PUBLIC_ prefix decides what gets into the client bundle.
Secrets stay private and server-only.

notEnough: Only saying you set env vars.

groups.title: End-to-End Testing with Playwright
groups.question: You want end-to-end tests for login and creating a post, without logging in at the start of every test. Explain how you would use Playwright.

followUps.Playwright installation and browser setu: What does Playwright run your tests against?
followUps.Writing page navigation and form interac: What would a good test for creating a post check?
followUps.Using Playwright fixtures and page objec: How do fixtures and page objects avoid repetition?

evidence.text: Playwright drives real Chromium, Firefox and WebKit browsers.
It has its own test runner.
Browsers are installed with Playwright's install command.
The test fills forms and clicks buttons like a user.
It asserts on the URL and what appears on the page.
It catches problems where parts work alone but fail together.
Page objects wrap selectors and actions for each page.
Fixtures provide ready setups, like an already logged-in browser.
Tests do not repeat login steps or selectors.

groups.title: Monitoring and Previews
groups.question: Reviewers want to see changes before merge, and production errors only show minified stack traces. Explain previews and error monitoring.

followUps.Preview deployments with adapter-vercel: What does a preview deployment give the team?
followUps.Sourcemaps and error monitoring in produ: Why upload source maps to Sentry?

evidence.text: Each pull request gets its own URL.
It runs the production build, often with staging settings.
Changes are tested before merging.
Monitoring tools capture production errors.
Production code is minified, so raw stack traces are unreadable.
Source maps translate them back to the original code.
